topic: Sharp cycle-flow bounds for coupled comparison-cohort anticipation. In finite staggered adoption under PT-All, let pre-adoption means satisfy mu_ht=alpha_h+lambda_t+a_ht, with a_ht zero outside known anticipation horizons and bounded inside them. Characterize the sharp joint fiber by the fundamental cycles of the cohort-time graph; prove a causal completion theorem for every compatible mean vector; give necessary and sufficient variation-independence and box-endpoint exactness frontiers; compute arbitrary ATT-aggregate endpoints using interval-tension feasibility and min-cost circulation; and construct finite-sample honest outer confidence sets by jointly optimizing simultaneous bounded-mean bands. The consumer is the Callaway-Sant'Anna not-yet-treated risk-set workflow for announced staggered policies, including the Indonesian anti-cheating rollout.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether every cycle-compatible bounded anticipation mean vector admits one announced-policy staggered-adoption potential-outcome law that preserves the observable distribution and PT-All while jointly realizing all overlapping not-yet-treated risk-set estimands and maintained outcome bounds.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked ancestor assumed the very compatibility needed for sharpness, so its support interval never established causal attainability. Cycle equations only show that conditional means admit an additive cohort-time representation; they do not construct one joint law indexed by announced adoption regimes, preserve observed-data consistency and PT-All across every reused comparison cohort, or enforce bounded outcome support. Piccininni, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and Stensrud make the intervention-indexing issue substantive, while Gong treats a smaller anticipation setting and Torgovitsky shows why full-law extension is load-bearing. The combined evidence leaves open whether cycle compatibility is sufficient or whether additional cross-regime inequalities are necessary.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A constructive causal-completion theorem mapping every feasible cycle-compatible mean vector to a joint bounded announced-policy potential-outcome law supporting all target group-time ATTs, or a smallest graph-regime counterexample with the missing necessary-and-sufficient compatibility condition.

writing_exemplar.why: Its intervention-first framing explains why an algebraically feasible mean table is not yet a coherent causal model.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: No anticipation depends on a named intervention -> announced and implemented policies induce distinct regimes -> overlapping risk sets must coexist in one law -> prove or refute causal completion

method_exemplars.technique: Lift feasible low-dimensional restrictions to a full admissible probability law by an explicit extension construction and prove that the observable projection is exhaustive.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required result must turn mean-level feasibility into existence of a common full-data law rather than infer sharpness from LP attainability.

method_exemplars.technique: Index potential outcomes by treatment timing and encode anticipatory behavior as a restricted causal response before implementation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a causal anticipation construction that can be enlarged from a classical DiD comparison to several announced adoption cohorts.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate group-time causal building blocks by outcome regression, IPW, or doubly robust scores and obtain simultaneous multiplier-bootstrap bands.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The completed law must support exactly the group-time ATT objects and overlapping not-yet-treated comparisons consumed by this workflow.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the sharp joint fiber of bounded comparison-cohort anticipation by the fundamental cycles of the cohort-time graph, including necessary-and-sufficient frontiers for primitive-box variation independence and coordinatewise endpoint exactness.

source_refs.claim: Sharp staggered-adoption bounds are derived cohort-by-cohort with never-treated controls; the not-yet-treated alternative is left to account for comparison-group anticipation.
source_refs.author: Gianna Fenaroli

open_problems.why_unsolved: Fenaroli's never-treated design separates cohort-specific sensitivity calculations, but a Callaway-Sant'Anna not-yet-treated risk set reuses the same pre-adoption cohort-time mean in several contrasts. The banked ancestor treated those primitives as a Cartesian box and explicitly deferred the configurations that couple them; the adjacent PT-All proposal identified only an abstract left-null-space restriction. The missing step is to identify that restriction with a fundamental-cycle system after clean coordinates are fixed, intersect it with heterogeneous edge intervals, and handle disconnected components and zero-width edges. Existing anticipation papers do not say when positive-width primitives remain freely variable or when cycle compatibility deletes nominal coordinate endpoints.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if theorem identifying the joint ATT-bias fiber as a fundamental-cycle affine system intersected with edge intervals, giving its dimension and nonemptiness certificate and exact graph criteria for full-box variation independence and attainment of each primitive endpoint.

writing_exemplar.why: Its transparent progression from bounded anticipation primitives to sharp staggered ATT bounds makes the nonseparable not-yet-treated case visible without changing the applied motivation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Policies induce bounded anticipatory responses -> sharp staggered bounds are separable with never-treated controls -> not-yet-treated reuse creates hidden compatibility -> characterize the cycle-coupled fiber and its frontiers

method_exemplars.technique: Formulate variation independence as surjectivity of a joint parameter range onto the product of its marginal ranges and isolate compatibility restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested bridge frontier is exactly a product-space versus constrained-image result for a graph-incidence parameterization.

method_exemplars.technique: Use graph incidence, connected components, and Laplacian structure to separate identified fixed-effect contrasts from component gauges.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The cohort and calendar effects form a two-way fixed-effect graph whose gauges and observable restrictions are controlled by the same connectivity algebra.

method_exemplars.technique: Obtain a joint asymptotic linear representation for group-time building blocks and simultaneous bootstrap bands.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once endpoint attainability is characterized, these are the observed risk-set quantities whose uncertainty enters the fiber.

open_problems.open_problem: For arbitrary signed aggregations of group-time ATTs under cycle-coupled bounded anticipation, derive sharp endpoint algorithms and dual certificates by reducing every support-function problem to interval-tension feasibility and minimum-cost circulation.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior support calculation pools repeated coordinates but then chooses each box coordinate independently according to its signed coefficient. Cycle equalities invalidate that first proof step. Generic partial-identification theory reduces the endpoint to an LP but does not expose the incidence structure, a violated-cycle feasibility certificate, or an attaining anticipation vector. The unresolved work is to dualize edge-interval tensions into node balances and capacities, prove equality with min-cost transshipment for arbitrary signed ATT weights, and cover component gauges, degeneracy, infeasible mean vectors, and optimizer-face changes. Targeted searches found no DiD paper using this circulation reduction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A primal-dual theorem equating every aggregate-ATT support endpoint from the cycle-fiber LP with a polynomial-time minimum-cost circulation or transshipment value, together with a necessary-and-sufficient negative-cycle or cut feasibility certificate and an attaining primal anticipation vector.

writing_exemplar.why: Its move from group-time effects to policy-relevant aggregations is the exact consumer narrative; the destination replaces point estimates of those summaries with sharp endpoints.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Staggered policies generate many group-time effects -> empirical conclusions use weighted summaries -> comparison anticipation jointly set-identifies the building blocks -> every summary needs a sharp auditable endpoint computation

method_exemplars.technique: Represent two-sided linear constraints as capacities and use primal-dual minimum-cost-flow machinery on the resulting balance equations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After incidence dualization, the sharp support calculation has exactly the balance, capacity, and linear-cost structure of minimum-cost circulation.

method_exemplars.technique: Treat a partially identified endpoint as a stochastic LP value, regularize the sample program, and derive limit theory allowing multiple optimizers.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each circulation endpoint is a structured LP value whose active optimal face can change with the cohort-time means.

method_exemplars.technique: Diagnose geometric regularity through constraint qualifications instead of assuming a smooth and stable optimizer.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The endpoint map is piecewise linear and changes derivative when the optimal circulation moves to another face.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct finite-sample honest outer confidence sets for the entire cycle-coupled ATT identified region by jointly optimizing simultaneous bounded-mean bands rather than bootstrapping separately estimated endpoints.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The bounded-anticipation ancestor stopped at population identification. Available staggered-DiD and functional event-study bands use asymptotic Gaussian or bootstrap approximations, while Fenaroli explains that its nonsmooth frontier can defeat regular frequentist inference and therefore gives Bayesian credible bands. Bounded school outcomes permit finite-sample simultaneous bands for primitive cohort-time means, but separately plugging those bands into endpoint formulas does not ensure outer coverage of a data-dependent polyhedral set and may miss infeasibility or active-face changes. The missing proof must propagate one joint high-probability mean event through feasibility and support optimization uniformly over compatible latent laws.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-sample theorem proving at least 1 − α coverage of the full population ATT identified set by the union of all cycle-feasible fibers over a simultaneous bounded-mean confidence region, with computable outer endpoints for every linear ATT aggregate.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames honest inference as simultaneous control of an entire event-study object, the right narrative for covering a whole identified region rather than isolated endpoints.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Event-study workflows invite many simultaneous claims -> pointwise uncertainty is not honest for the whole object -> simultaneous bands repair multiplicity asymptotically -> bounded outcomes permit finite-sample outer coverage after joint cycle-feasibility optimization

method_exemplars.technique: Construct nonasymptotic tail bounds for bounded cohort-time sample means and combine them into one simultaneous confidence event.
method_exemplars.why_closest: On this event the unknown population mean vector belongs to the same deterministic optimization that defines the outer identified set.

method_exemplars.technique: Define the partial-identification coverage target explicitly and protect validity as the width of the identified set approaches zero.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Cycle fibers include point-identified forests and positive-width cyclic cases, so coverage must survive changing identification width.

method_exemplars.technique: Organize estimation around the joint vector of group-time ATT building blocks and report simultaneous rather than pointwise uncertainty.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the risk-set sampling architecture and downstream aggregations while the new proof replaces its asymptotic bootstrap layer.

literature_map:
Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1803.09015) identify group-time ATTs with never- or not-yet-treated controls, aggregate them, and give asymptotic simultaneous bands.
Goodman-Bacon (2021, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2021.03.014) exposes the comparison structure of staggered TWFE but maintains clean preperiods.
Sun and Abraham (2021, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.09.006) and Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess (2024, Review of Economic Studies, DOI 10.1093/restud/rdae007) repair heterogeneous-effect event studies under no anticipation.
Roth et al. (2023, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2023.03.008) call no anticipation an important, often hidden identifying assumption.
Gong (2022, arXiv:2111.06573) gives anticipation bounds beginning from a classical DiD model.
Fenaroli (2026, arXiv:2603.00868) derives sharp joint anticipation/PT bounds; its staggered extension uses never-treated controls and leaves not-yet-treated controls to account for comparison anticipation.
Augustin, Gutknecht, and Liu (2025, arXiv:2507.20415) analyze staggered anticipation as misspecification, correct using timing knowledge and unaffected groups, and revisit Indonesian anti-cheating.
Piccininni, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and Stensrud (2025, arXiv:2507.12891) expose intervention ambiguity in no-anticipation statements.
Berkhout et al. (2024, Journal of Development Economics, DOI 10.1016/j.jdeveco.2024.103307) provide the announced phased Indonesian computer-testing application and report pre-adoption responses.
Rambachan and Roth (2023, Review of Economic Studies, DOI 10.1093/restud/rdad018) give robust event-study inference for bounded trend violations while maintaining no anticipation.
Fang and Liebl (2026, arXiv:2512.06804) give asymptotic honest functional event-study bands but do not derive a coupled identification region.
Torgovitsky (2019, Quantitative Economics, DOI 10.3982/QE634) illustrates why sharpness needs a full-law completion or extension proof.
Voronin (2025, arXiv:2503.14940) develops identification and pointwise inference for generic LP-valued sharp bounds and identifies uniformity restrictions.
Imbens and Manski (2004, Econometrica, DOI 10.1111/j.1468-0262.2004.00555.x) and Hoeffding (1963, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.1963.10500830) supply the partial-ID coverage target and bounded-mean concentration ingredient.
Targeted searches found no econometric paper characterizing coupled anticipation by cohort-time cycles, bridge-based variation independence, interval tensions, or minimum-cost circulation.
